quickAnswer.question: What skills should a frontend developer put on a resume?
quickAnswer.answer: Frontend developer and frontend engineer roles look for the same core skills. Lead with the fundamentals every team expects — JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML and CSS — then your primary framework (usually React), plus proof you can ship quality: testing, version control, API integration and performance. Tailor the exact mix to the job you're targeting.

categories.title: Languages & Markup
categories.lead: The non-negotiable foundation. List the ones you use confidently — add depth in parentheses where you can, e.g. “JavaScript (ES6+)”.

categories.title: Frameworks & Meta-frameworks

categories.title: APIs & Integration

categories.title: Build Tools & Tooling

categories.title: Testing & Quality

categories.title: Performance & Optimization
categories.lead: Higher signal when you can back it with a measurable result — pick the ones you’ve actually moved a number with.

skillsToAvoid.heading: Skills you usually don't need to list
skillsToAvoid.description: For modern frontend roles these are assumed — including them dilutes your stronger skills. Leave them off unless a specific posting explicitly asks.

faq.q: How many skills should a frontend developer put on a resume?
faq.a: Aim for 10–15 well-chosen skills. Enough to cover the fundamentals and the specific technologies a job asks for, but curated to what you can actually discuss in an interview. A wall of 40 tools reads as noise and dilutes your strongest signals.

faq.q: Is a frontend developer the same as a frontend engineer?
faq.a: In most companies, yes — "frontend developer" and "frontend engineer" are used interchangeably for the same role, and job postings mix the two freely. "Engineer" sometimes signals a little more emphasis on architecture, testing and performance, but the core skills are the same. Every skill on this page applies whether the posting says frontend developer or frontend engineer.

faq.q: What are the most important frontend developer skills?
faq.a: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML and CSS are the non-negotiable foundation, followed by a primary framework (usually React). Beyond those, employers look for testing, version control with Git, API integration, responsive design, and performance optimization.

faq.q: Should frontend developers list soft skills?
faq.a: Yes, but sparingly and in context. Rather than a generic "communication", show it in a work-experience bullet — collaborating with designers and product managers to ship a feature. A few contextual soft skills beat a long list of generic ones.

faq.q: Should I list React as a resume skill?
faq.a: If you use it, absolutely — React is one of the most in-demand frontend skills and a frequent ATS keyword. Make it more specific where you can: "React (Hooks, component architecture, performance optimization)" signals far more depth than "React" alone.

faq.q: What skills should a junior frontend developer include?
faq.a: Focus on the fundamentals you can demonstrate: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, a framework like React, Git, and responsive design. Back each with a project or bullet. At entry level, depth in the basics beats a long list of tools you've only tried once.

faq.q: How do I tailor frontend skills to a job description?
faq.a: Read the posting and note the specific skills it names. Mirror those — in your own true words — and move them toward the top of your skills section. Applicant tracking systems rank you partly on how well your resume echoes the job's language, so relevant, honest overlap matters.
